iteration_focus: Focused re-check of three iteration-3 fixes: (1) Task 4 two-try-block decrypt shape, (2) Task 5 positive-path IT must use real tokenEncryptor.encrypt ciphertext, (3) Task 9 scenario catalog count reconciliation (28 unit / 38 total).

fix_1_task4_two_try_block_decrypt.description: Task 4 iter-3 fix: Base64 decode in its own try/catch(IllegalArgumentException) -> BotTokenInvalidException; tokenEncryptor.decrypt(iv,ct) placed OUTSIDE that catch so its IllegalArgumentException (wrong-IV-length, line 46-49 of TokenEncryptor.java) and IllegalStateException (AEAD failure, lines 56-57) both propagate as 500.

token_encryptor_line_46_49.actual_code: if (iv == null || iv.length != IV_BYTES) throw new IllegalArgumentException('AES-GCM IV must be exactly ' + IV_BYTES + ' bytes; got ...')
token_encryptor_line_46_49.throws: IllegalArgumentException on bad IV length — NOT GeneralSecurityException and NOT IllegalStateException
token_encryptor_line_46_49.implication: A single catch(IllegalArgumentException) wrapping both Base64.decode AND tokenEncryptor.decrypt would incorrectly catch the wrong-IV-length signal and convert a storage-corruption 500 into a user-facing 422 invalid_bot_token. The two-try-block shape is the ONLY correct implementation.

token_encryptor_line_56_57.actual_code: throw new IllegalStateException('AES-GCM decryption failed', e) inside catch(GeneralSecurityException e)
token_encryptor_line_56_57.covers: Both tampered ciphertext (AEADBadTagException) and all other GeneralSecurityException subclasses — wraps into IllegalStateException, propagates as 500 via GlobalErrorHandler.
